declarations.docstring: Over any ring, Ext in degree zero is additively equivalent to the group of module homomorphisms.
Over any ring, Tor in degree zero is the balanced tensor product of the right module and the left module.
Provides the stated additive equivalence at degree one for the module data.
The long exact Ext sequence in the second argument is exact across two adjacent degrees.
For a short exact sequence of left modules, construct the connecting Tor map and prove exactness of the five adjacent arrows.
Tor can be computed by resolving either factor: compare the derived tensor functors on right modules and on left modules.
The long exact Ext sequence in the first argument reverses arrows and is exact across two adjacent degrees.
For a short exact sequence of right modules, construct the connecting Tor map and prove exactness of the five adjacent arrows.
Defines the comparison isomorphism from degree zero to the left-derived functor value.
States naturality of the degree-zero comparison isomorphism with respect to a morphism.
Builds a degree-one cocycle from a morphism whose displayed composite vanishes.
For an algebra over a field, identify Ext¹(W, V) with the extension-cocycle quotient classifying extensions of W by V.
Describes the value of the displayed degree-one additive equivalence on an element.
Computes the displayed degree-one equivalence on an extension built from a cocycle.
States commutativity of the natural comparison square at degree zero.
Constructs an isomorphism between the middle objects of an exact five-arrow diagram with zero outer objects.
Shows that the displayed morphisms associated to a short complex have zero composite.
Obtains an exact five-arrow sequence by applying the displayed left-derived maps to a short exact complex.
